system_prompt_style.note: Prompt is rebuilt every step from system prompt, current state context and step prompt via PromptsHandler. Line number not given in the evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Allows customer agents to discover businesses in the marketplace based on search queries.
env_context_strategy.note: The environment is a marketplace, not a code repository. The agent discovers businesses through the Search action.

context_compaction.note: The prompts.py and base agent code were not included in the evidence.

observation_format.note: Observations are formatted into text history. Structured objects are dumped into text strings.

tool_call_format.note: The agent chooses an action through a structured-output CustomerAction model rather than a tool-call API. This is the closest value.

tool_count.note: The CustomerAction model (customer/models.py) is not in the evidence. The paper describes 5 protocol actions.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote:
Our protocol consists of 5 unique actions: search, send-
ing text messages, sending order proposals, sending pay-
ments, and fetching new messages.
edit_primitive.note: The action space has no file-editing action.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: /actions/protocol` - Agents get the message protocol from the platform
tool_schema_source.note: Actions are Pydantic models and the platform serves their schemas. The schema-producing code was not shown.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote:
Magentic Marketplaceextends this landscape by
proposing a transaction-oriented protocol
protocol_standardization.note: The system uses its own HTTP marketplace protocol, not MCP or A2A. No grep for mcp/a2a was available; the paper mentions MCP only as an analogy. 'none' is also plausible.

loop_primitives.note: The customer agent runs an LLM-decide, execute, observe loop. Businesses poll for messages. The paper calls these baseline ReACT-style agents.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: # Use LLM to decide next action
planning_granularity.note: No plan object appears in the evidence.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Sends a message from one agent to another.
multi_agent_topology.note: Many customer and business agents exchange messages through a central platform server.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: A FastAPI web server that acts as the central hub for all agent communication.

human_in_loop.note: The paper only discusses HITL as a future direction. No config surface for it was shown.

short_term_state.note: State also includes completed_transactions and an event_history.

long_term_memory.note: The paper says the experiments used static markets without learning. No memory config surface was shown.

state_persistence.note: The run and experiment code was not shown. Only --override-db appears.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: # FUTURE -- add retries on message fail.
retry_policy.note: This comment concerns message sends. Task-level retries do not appear in the step loop.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: if self._max_steps is not None and self.conversation_step >= self._max_steps:
termination_condition.note: The CLI default is 100 steps. A model-declared end-transaction action is suggested in the step docstring but its code was truncated.

cost_controls.note: This is a per-response cap rather than a run budget. A concurrency limit also exists.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote:
Agents operate as independent clients while the marketplace environ-
ment serves as the central server
execution_isolation.note: Agent actions are HTTP calls to a local server. Docker runs only the database.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Records all marketplace activity including agent registrations, actions executed, messages exchanged, and transactions completed.
filesystem_access.note: Agents have no filesystem actions. They act only on the simulated marketplace state.

permission_model.note: The platform protocol validates actions, but the code was not shown.

tracing.evidence_quote: **logs**: Captures agent decision-making processes and LLM interactions
tracing.note: Actions are recorded in a Postgres/SQLite database.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: After an experiment finishes, you can analyze the results with this command.
eval_hooks.note: Welfare analytics are built into the CLI.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Magentic Marketplace is a Python SDK for running simulations of agentic markets.
target_domain.note: The domain is simulation of agentic economic marketplaces.
